Q: Invalid column type from bcp client for colid A:

Invalid column type from bcp client for colid 1.

The above error message can occur when the table already exists in the target database and the table definition in Node via table.columns.add(...) does not match the actual definition in SQL Server.

In the comments it was mentioned that the giver_id column is varchar(max) so a matching definition in Node would be:

table.columns.add('giver_id', sql.VarChar(sql.MAX), { nullable: false });

Q: Is it ok to run Docker from inside Docker? A:

Running Docker inside Docker (a.k.a. DinD), while possible, should be avoided, if at all possible. (Source provided below.) Instead, you want to set up a way for your main container to produce and communicate with sibling containers.

Jérôme Petazzoni — the author of the feature that made it possible for Docker to run inside a Docker container — actually wrote a blog post saying not to do it. The use case he describes matches the OP's exact use case of a CI Docker container that needs to run jobs inside other Docker containers.

Petazzoni lists two reasons why DinD is troublesome:

  1. It does not cooperate well with Linux Security Modules (LSM).
  2. It creates a mismatch in file systems that creates problems for the containers created inside parent containers.

From that blog post, he describes the following alternative:

[The] simplest way is to just expose the Docker socket to your CI container, by bind-mounting it with the -v flag.

Simply put, when you start your CI container (Jenkins or other), instead of hacking something together with Docker-in-Docker, start it with:

docker run -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock ...

Now this container will have access to the Docker socket, and will therefore be able to start containers. Except that instead of starting "child" containers, it will start "sibling" containers.

Q: Created a Moodle website using google API account login working since last two years but now it stop working A:

The callback url is working, its displaying a session time out error with the parameters above, which is correct

So I'm guessing this error is displayed on the Google website not the Moodle website?

Double check the Google settings are correct and enabled

There are some instructions here

https://docs.moodle.org/401/en/OAuth_2_Google_service

Start by going to https://console.developers.google.com/

Then select your project > Credentials > OAuth 2.0 Client IDs

Check its enabled

The url should be https://seed.jss.ph.education/admin/oauth2callback.php

Note it should be https not http

If that looks okay, then maybe double check the client id and client secret are correct in Moodle

Site admin > Server > OAuth2 services > Google

The default for the service base url is https://accounts.google.com/

Q: Why is Chrome showing a "Please Fill Out this Field" tooltip on empty fields? A:

Problem

Using HTML5 form validation (required, type="email", etc.) can block form submission before any JavaScript submit handlers run.

In a server-rendered setup (e.g. Django templates), this becomes a problem when:

  • Validation is performed server-side

  • The page must reload to render validation errors

  • The browser’s native tooltip (“Please fill out this field”) prevents submission entirely

Adding novalidate directly to the form did not work in this case because it interfered with existing validation logic and submission flow.

Important behavior to understand

HTML5 form validation runs before the submit event is dispatched.

If the form is invalid:

  • The browser blocks submission

  • The submit event is never fired

  • submit event listeners and preventDefault() never run

This explains why JavaScript attached to submit appears to “do nothing”.

Solution: disable HTML5 validation just before submission

Intercept the user interaction before the browser runs native validation, and disable it at that moment.

This approach:

  • Allows the form to submit normally

  • Preserves full page reloads

  • Keeps server-side validation intact

Global solution (drop into base.html)

<script>
  document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
    // Mouse / touch submit
    document.addEventListener("click", e => {
      const btn = e.target.closest(
        "button[type='submit'], input[type='submit']"
      );
      if (!btn) return;

      const form = btn.closest("form");
      if (form) form.noValidate = true;
    });

    // Enter-key submit
    document.addEventListener("keydown", e => {
      if (e.key !== "Enter") return;

      const form = e.target.closest("form");
      if (form) form.noValidate = true;
    });
  });
</script>

Why this works

  • click and keydown events fire before HTML5 validation

  • form.noValidate = true disables native validation just in time

  • The browser proceeds with a normal form submission

  • Django receives the POST and renders validation errors as usual

Why this solution is elegant

  • ✅ No template changes

  • ✅ No novalidate attribute scattered across files

  • ✅ Preserves server-side validation

  • ✅ Works with full-page reloads

  • ✅ Browser-agnostic

  • ✅ Plays nicely with legacy code

Summary

If you rely on server-side validation and page reloads, disabling HTML5 validation at submit time (instead of globally) avoids browser interference while keeping your existing logic intact.

Sometimes the correct fix is simply telling HTML5 validation:

“Thanks, but I’ve got this.” 😄

P.S. Thanks to ChatGPT for the help on this one!
